comments.body:
Implemented and pushed for review: https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1018 (commit 571f6d2ab, branch 7ab3-structural-link-comparability).

What landed in the change:
- resolve_hierarchy_link now resolves blocking pairs via the nearest common ancestor of the two endpoints. _get_ancestors terminates every chain with a _VIRTUAL_ROOT sentinel, so parentless tickets are siblings and there is no undefined disjoint-tree case; a new _resolve_blocking_endpoints helper does the NCA lookup and returns (resolved_source, resolved_target, is_ancestor_pair).
- _get_ancestors lost its max_hops=2 cap and gained a visited-set cycle guard.
- _TYPE_TIER, _tier_of, _tier_of_ticket and _promote_to_tier deleted; grep over src/ and tests/ confirms zero remaining references.
- is_redundant is recomputed from the RESOLVED pair inside the blocking branch only. The non-blocking early return keeps the original-pair value untouched, so relates_to / duplicates / supersedes / discovered_from / caused_by gain no new rejections.
- Rejection wording widened in _links.py and in composer._link_dry_run; no new branch was needed in either, since both already handle is_redundant.
- Six prose sites updated (link.txt, ticket-model.md, event-schema.md, cli-reference.md, user-guide.md, plus the ticket-model section heading).

Two findings from implementation that the plan did not anticipate:

1. A self-loop (source == target) was being swallowed by the ancestor check and raised ValueError("redundant link") instead of CyclicDependencyError, breaking test_add_dependency_raises_on_self_loop_at_level. A ticket is not its own ancestor, so _resolve_blocking_endpoints now returns identical endpoints untouched and lets the existing cycle guard handle them. This was NOT in the plan and was caught only by the existing suite.

2. The predicted three-test inversion held exactly. SC3, SC5 and the parametrised cousins case changed and produced precisely the predicted endpoints; the other eight resolver tests passed unmodified, including both halves of the former type-tier fallback test (renamed, assertions untouched) and test_resolve_hierarchy_link_is_redundant_direct_parent.

Verification: pytest tests/scripts/graph/ = 74 passed. Full tests/unit + tests/scripts + tests/interfaces = 7479 passed, 32 skipped; the 2 reported errors were a REPO_ROOT-leak guard tripping on a .mypy_cache created by a concurrent make typecheck in the same worktree, and both files pass clean when re-run alone. make lint and make typecheck both pass. _hierarchy.py is 282 lines, well under the 800 cap.

Not yet done: awaiting LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 before submit; ticket stays in_progress until the change merges and the worktree is fast-forwarded.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

`resolve_hierarchy_link` (`src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py:98`) promotes blocking links (`blocks` / `depends_on`) so both endpoints sit at a "comparable level", but it defines that level by ticket TYPE TIER — `_TYPE_TIER` at `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py:26` maps epic to 2, story to 1, task/bug to 0. Two consequences, both reported as bugs against this story's parent:

Bug 1803-df54-18bb-4881: a task T and a story S that are both direct children of epic E cannot hold a direct dependency. Linking `T depends_on S` promotes T toward tier 1, `_promote_to_tier` (`src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py:77`) walks T's chain `[T, E]`, finds no story-tier ancestor because E is tier 2, and takes the chain-root fallback at `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py:93` — returning E. The store records `E depends_on S`, an epic blocked by its own child, and the requested T-to-S edge is never written.

Bug jira-reb-1582: comparability should key on the parent hierarchy, not on type. Any two tickets under the same parent may hold a dependency; a cross-subtree dependency escalates to the nearest common ancestor's children.

A second defect compounds this. `add_dependency` (`src/rebar/graph/_links.py:180`) rejects redundant links, but `is_redundant` is computed by the resolver at `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py:167` from the ORIGINAL source and target, before promotion. `T depends_on S` is not redundant; the promoted `E depends_on S` is, and nothing re-checks it after promotion. Nothing anywhere validates the pair that actually gets written, which is why the guard that should have caught 1803 never saw the offending pair.

## Approach

Replace type-tier comparability with structural comparability, and evaluate the redundancy guard on the pair that is actually written.

**Structural rule (blocking relations).** Stated as the branch set the implementer writes, so the disjoint case is an explicit outcome rather than an undefined NCA:

1. Build the full ancestor chain of each endpoint, ordered self-first, and append a **virtual root** sentinel: `[self, parent, …, root, VIRTUAL_ROOT]`. The sentinel encodes jira-reb-1582's rule that "Tickets with no parent are considered siblings for this purpose" — every real root is a child of the virtual root, so a common ancestor always exists and there is no undefined disjoint case.
2. Let `NCA` be the first id in the source chain that also appears in the target chain. With the sentinel this always succeeds; in the worst case `NCA` is `VIRTUAL_ROOT`.
3. If `NCA` equals either endpoint, one is an ancestor of the other; skip escalation and let the redundancy guard below reject it.
4. Otherwise escalate each endpoint to the element of its own chain immediately preceding `NCA` — its ancestor that is a direct child of `NCA`. When an endpoint is already a direct child of `NCA`, that element is the endpoint itself and it is unchanged.

Two direct children of the same parent hit step 4 with both elements unchanged, and link as-is with `was_redirected` false. Two parentless roots have chains `[A, VIRTUAL_ROOT]` and `[B, VIRTUAL_ROOT]`, so `NCA` is `VIRTUAL_ROOT` and step 4 leaves both unchanged — roots are siblings, as specified. `VIRTUAL_ROOT` is an internal sentinel only; it is never a resolved endpoint, because step 4 always returns the element *preceding* the NCA.

**Cousins now escalate — an intended behaviour change, not a side effect.** Under the type-tier rule two leaf tickets are always "comparable" (task and bug are both tier 0), so a dependency between cousins in different sub-trees records directly. Under the structural rule their NCA is the shared grandparent, so each escalates to its own parent. jira-reb-1582 specifies exactly this: "Dependency links outside of the same parent must escalate to the closest shared parent."

Walking the existing suite in `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_hierarchy_resolve.py` against the algorithm above, exactly THREE tests change and the rest hold. To be inverted, not deleted:

- `test_resolve_hierarchy_link_cross_story_same_epic_sc3` (line 61) — `task-a1` / `task-b1` across `story-a` / `story-b` under one epic. Becomes `story-a` to `story-b`, `was_redirected` true.
- `test_resolve_hierarchy_link_cross_epic_sc5` (line 107) — `task-a1` / `task-b1` in separate epics. NCA is `VIRTUAL_ROOT`, so it becomes `epic-a` to `epic-b`, `was_redirected` true.
- `test_resolve_hierarchy_link_same_tier_siblings_cousins_not_promoted` (line 327), parametrised over task/bug pairs — becomes `story-a` to `story-b`, `was_redirected` true, and is renamed since its current name asserts the opposite.

The other eight hold unchanged, which is the main evidence that the virtual-root formulation is right rather than merely convenient. In particular `test_resolve_hierarchy_link_task_to_epic_promotes_to_epic` (line 270) still yields `epic-root` to `epic-other`, `test_resolve_hierarchy_link_task_to_story_promotes_to_story` (line 302) still yields `story-mid` to `story-other`, and both halves of `test_resolve_hierarchy_link_fallback_no_comparable_ancestor` (line 356) still hold — the orphan pair unchanged, and `story-task` still escalating to `lone-story` — even though that test was written to exercise the tier fallback being deleted. Its name no longer describes what it checks, so it is renamed to reflect virtual-root escalation while its assertions stay as they are.

This widens escalation relative to today, so more cross-subtree dependencies will surface a redirect record — which is the loud signal the design deliberately keeps.

**Redundancy guard, evaluated post-resolution.** For blocking relations `is_redundant` becomes "the RESOLVED pair is in an ancestor-descendant relationship, in either direction" — which subsumes the direct parent-child case it covers today, since a parent is an ancestor. This single change closes both halves of the defect: the direct parent-child request still rejects exactly as it does now (resolved pair equals original pair), and 1803's escalated `E depends_on S` now rejects too, because E is S's ancestor.

Reusing `is_redundant` rather than introducing a new `{"error": ...}` return is deliberate. The resolver already has an error channel for *unusable input* — missing, unreducible, or non-graph-artifact endpoints — whereas an ancestor-blocking pair is well-formed input describing an invalid edge, which is precisely what `is_redundant` already reports. The existing comment at `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py:163` gives the rationale that extends to the general case: the hierarchy edge already expresses the relationship, so a blocking edge layered on it adds nothing. Keeping one channel also means `add_dependency` needs no new branch (`src/rebar/graph/_links.py:180` already raises `ValueError` on it), `_link_dry_run` needs no new branch (`src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:635` already prints a rejection for it), and the two existing tests that pin this behaviour — `test_resolve_hierarchy_link_is_redundant_direct_parent` (`tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_hierarchy_resolve.py:213`) and the `add_dependency` redundancy case (`tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_hierarchy_adddep.py:88`) — keep passing unmodified, because a direct parent-child pair satisfies the widened predicate too.

**Non-blocking relations keep today's `is_redundant` exactly.** It is computed at `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py:167` before the non-blocking early return at `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py:170`, so it is part of the response for `relates_to` / `duplicates` / `supersedes` / `discovered_from` / `caused_by` as well. Those relations are not escalated and must not gain new rejections, so the widened predicate applies only inside the blocking branch; the non-blocking branch keeps returning the original-pair direct-parent-child answer.

Concretely, this restructures the one shared variable at `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py:167` into two computations. The existing line stays where it is and keeps its current expression, and its value continues to be returned by the non-blocking early return at `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py:170` unchanged. Inside the blocking branch the value is then RECOMPUTED from `resolved_source` / `resolved_target` as an ancestor-descendant test, and only that recomputed value reaches the blocking branch's return at `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py:223`. The ancestor test reuses the chains already built for NCA resolution — one endpoint is an ancestor of the other exactly when it appears in the other's chain — so it costs no extra reduces.

**Ancestor walk.** `_get_ancestors` (`src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py:41`) is capped at `max_hops=2`, which truncates any chain deeper than epic to story to task and feeds the same chain-root fallback that produced 1803. Remove the cap and walk to the root, guarding with a visited set so a malformed parent cycle terminates instead of looping.

**Deletions.** `_TYPE_TIER`, `_tier_of`, `_tier_of_ticket` and `_promote_to_tier` become dead once comparability is structural. Removal is safe because all four are private to `_hierarchy.py` and referenced nowhere else: `grep -rn` for each name across `src/` and `tests/`, excluding `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py` itself, returns no matches. The package `__all__` (`src/rebar/graph/__init__.py:28`) re-exports only `resolve_hierarchy_link` and `compute_archive_eligible` from this module, so none of the four is part of the package surface.

**Escalation is retained**, including the machine-readable redirect record composed at `src/rebar/graph/_links.py:207`. Rejected alternative: refuse cross-subtree blocking links outright so nothing is ever silently substituted. It is the more honest contract, but it breaks existing callers that rely on auto-escalation — the `link` MCP tool, and the reconciler's inbound apply path, which calls `rebar.link` at `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py:502` under a fail-open `except Exception` — and jira-reb-1582 explicitly specifies escalation, not rejection.

The non-graph-artifact refusal at `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py:183` is unchanged: `session_log` / `code_review` still cannot be blocking endpoints.

## Out of scope (deferred, not dropped)

This ticket changes what a NEW link means. It does NOT repair blocking edges already written to the store under the type-tier rule — an epic already holding `depends_on` on its own child stays on disk until repaired, because a `LINK` event is durable and nothing re-resolves it on read. That store-wide audit and one-shot repair is the sibling ticket 9ad7-d5a2-a664-4827 (`rebar link-audit`), which declares `depends_on` on this ticket because its repair re-resolves each existing edge through the resolver this ticket delivers. The two are deliberately separate changes: this one is a semantics change reviewable in isolation; that one is a store-wide data rewrite whose correctness depends on these semantics being settled first.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py` — rewrite `resolve_hierarchy_link`'s blocking branch to NCA resolution; compute `is_redundant` for that branch from the resolved pair as an ancestor-descendant test; uncap and cycle-guard `_get_ancestors`; delete `_TYPE_TIER`, `_tier_of`, `_tier_of_ticket`, `_promote_to_tier`. The non-blocking branch and its `is_redundant` are untouched.
- `src/rebar/graph/_links.py` — widen only the rejection MESSAGE at `src/rebar/graph/_links.py:181`, which currently reads "are in a direct parent-child relationship", to name the ancestor-descendant case. The control flow at `src/rebar/graph/_links.py:180` is unchanged; the existing test matches on the word "redundant", which the new message keeps.
- `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py` — update the `_link_dry_run` rejection wording at `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:636`, which currently says "redundant link (direct child)", to name the ancestor-descendant case. No new branch: `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:635` already branches on `is_redundant`, and no new response key is introduced.
- `src/rebar/_cli/help/link.txt` — line 3 describes promotion "to a comparable hierarchy level"; restate as the structural rule.
- `docs/ticket-model.md` — the "Hierarchy promotion (blocking links only)" section at line 130 documents the epic/story/task tier rule; rewrite for the structural rule.
- `docs/cli-reference.md` (line 236) and `docs/user-guide.md` (line 169) — the same promotion sentence, kept consistent.
- `docs/event-schema.md` — the `LINK` / `UNLINK` row at line 51 states the promotion rule as "between comparable levels (epic↔epic, story↔story, task/bug↔task/bug)"; restate structurally. Its adjacent note that `UNLINK` must target the promoted endpoint stays true and is kept.
- `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_hierarchy_resolve.py` — resolver cases; existing type-tier expectations updated to the structural rule.
- `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_hierarchy_adddep.py` — `add_dependency` cases, including the 1803 repro and the post-resolution rejection.

## Testing

- Happy path: two direct children of the same parent link `depends_on` with no promotion, `was_redirected` false and `is_redundant` false.
- Happy path: two tickets with no parent link unchanged, treated as siblings under the virtual root.
- Edge: a leaf deep in one tree linked to a root in a disjoint tree escalates to that leaf's own root, not to the virtual sentinel — the sentinel never appears as a resolved endpoint.
- Edge (bug 1803 repro): task T and story S both direct children of epic E — `T depends_on S` records T to S exactly, `was_redirected` is false, and no epic-to-child edge is written.
- Edge (jira-reb-1582 worked example): Epic A parents Story C and Task B; Story C parents Task D. `D depends_on B` escalates to `C depends_on B`; `B depends_on C` records directly with no escalation.
- Edge: a chain deeper than two hops (epic to story to task to sub-task) escalates to the correct NCA children rather than to the chain root, which the old `max_hops=2` cap made impossible.
- Failure: a blocking link whose RESOLVED pair is ancestor-descendant but whose ORIGINAL pair is not — the shape that escaped the old guard — is reported `is_redundant` and raises from `add_dependency`.
- Failure: a blocking link between a grandparent and its grandchild is rejected, not merely the direct parent-child case.
- Failure: a malformed parent cycle in the ancestor walk terminates rather than hanging.
- Edge (cousins): two leaf tickets in different stories under one epic escalate to those stories, with `was_redirected` true — inverting the two existing tests named in the Approach.
- Regression: the two existing redundancy tests pass unmodified.
- Regression: non-blocking relations (`relates_to`, `supersedes`, `discovered_from`) still record the exact pair with `was_redirected` false, gain no new rejections, and blocking links to a `session_log` are still refused.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `T depends_on S` where T (task) and S (story) are both direct children of epic E records exactly one edge, T to S, and no edge on E; verified by the new case in `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_hierarchy_adddep.py`.
- [ ] `D depends_on B` resolves to `C depends_on B` and `B depends_on C` resolves unchanged, for the Epic A / Story C / Task B / Task D fixture; verified by the new case in `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_hierarchy_resolve.py`.
- [ ] A blocking pair whose resolved endpoints are grandparent and grandchild returns `is_redundant` true and makes `add_dependency` raise `ValueError`; verified by the new failure cases in both graph test files.
- [ ] `test_resolve_hierarchy_link_is_redundant_direct_parent` and the `add_dependency` redundancy case pass with no edits to either test body; verified by `git diff` over `tests/scripts/graph/` showing neither test function modified.
- [ ] A `relates_to` link between a grandparent and grandchild is still recorded, gaining no rejection from the widened blocking predicate; verified by a new non-blocking case in `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_hierarchy_resolve.py`.
- [ ] `_TYPE_TIER`, `_tier_of`, `_tier_of_ticket` and `_promote_to_tier` are absent from the tree; verified by `grep -rn -e _TYPE_TIER -e _tier_of -e _tier_of_ticket -e _promote_to_tier src/ tests/ --include='*.py'` returning no matches.
- [ ] A four-level chain escalates to the NCA children rather than the chain root; verified by the new deep-chain case in `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_hierarchy_resolve.py`.
- [ ] `task-a1 blocks task-b1` across `story-a` / `story-b` under one epic resolves to `story-a blocks story-b` with `was_redirected` true; verified by the inverted `test_resolve_hierarchy_link_cross_story_same_epic_sc3` and the renamed cousins test in `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_hierarchy_resolve.py`.
- [ ] Exactly the three tests named in the Approach are modified in `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_hierarchy_resolve.py`, and the other eight retain their existing assertions; verified by `git diff tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_hierarchy_resolve.py` touching only those three test bodies plus the two renames and the new cases.
- [ ] No resolved endpoint is ever the virtual-root sentinel; verified by the new disjoint-tree case asserting the resolved ids are both real ticket ids.
- [ ] `_get_ancestors` terminates on a parent cycle instead of looping; verified by the new cycle-guard case in `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_hierarchy_resolve.py`, which builds a fixture whose parent pointers form a loop and asserts the call returns.
- [ ] `src/rebar/_cli/help/link.txt`, `docs/ticket-model.md`, `docs/cli-reference.md`, `docs/user-guide.md` and `docs/event-schema.md` no longer describe the epic/story/task tier rule; verified by `grep -rn -e "comparable hierarchy level" -e "epic↔epic" src/rebar/_cli/help/link.txt docs/` returning no matches.
- [ ] Each of those five files positively describes the structural rule; verified by `grep -rln "nearest common ancestor" src/rebar/_cli/help/link.txt docs/ticket-model.md docs/cli-reference.md docs/user-guide.md docs/event-schema.md` listing all five paths.
- [ ] `rebar link <a> <b> depends_on --dry-run` for a pair whose resolved endpoints are ancestor-descendant prints a `[DRY RUN] Would reject` line naming the ancestor-descendant case, and writes no event; verified by the new dry-run case in `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_hierarchy_adddep.py`.
- [ ] An escalated cross-subtree link reports `was_redirected` true and `add_dependency` emits the redirect JSON record to stdout; verified by the existing `test_add_dependency_cross_story_emits_redirect_json_to_stdout` in `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_hierarchy_adddep.py` continuing to pass, updated only for the new resolved endpoints.
- [ ] `pytest tests/scripts/graph/`, `make lint` and `make typecheck` all pass in the worktree; verified by running each.
- [ ] `src/rebar/graph/_hierarchy.py` remains under the 800-line module cap; verified by `wc -l`.
